title: Research: which Shizuku settings does FleetProfileApplier miss?
description:
SCOPE — RESEARCH/RECOMMENDATION ONLY, NOT A CODE-CHANGE TASK. Do not modify any files in the Shizuku repo. Do not run any device/adb commands. Do not touch ~/src/Shizuku (that's a separate, unrelated standalone checkout — see ops-djbclark-bc9, explicitly hands-off, do not confuse with this task). Deliverable is a recommendation posted via 'bd comment ops-djbclark-bk7.1 --file <path>' (or 'bd comment ops-djbclark-bk7.1 "..."' directly) on this task itself — no GitHub issue exists for this yet, do not create one. Do not close the parent epic or any other bead besides this one.

Context: manager/src/main/java/moe/shizuku/manager/fleet/FleetProfileApplier.kt (150 lines) applies a JSON 'fleet profile' to a device's Shizuku settings via SharedPreferences, but only recognizes 8 hardcoded keys (see its 'knownKeys' set: mode, start_on_boot, watchdog, tcp_mode, tcp_port, auto_disable_usb_debugging, legacy_pairing, update_mode). Anything else in the profile JSON is silently skipped with an 'Unknown key' error collected in the Result. HANDOFF.md's 'Known issues & limitations' table flags this as untested-on-real-device and limited in scope.

Questions to investigate and answer with a clear recommendation (not just present tradeoffs):
- What is the full surface of settings/preferences Shizuku's manager app actually exposes (find wherever preference keys/settings are defined in this codebase, likely a settings/preferences class -- search broadly, the exact file name/location is unknown going in)?
- Of those, which are meaningfully fleet-relevant (things an operator would plausibly want to set programmatically across many devices) vs. purely UI/per-device state that wouldn't make sense in a pushed profile?
- For any settings that ARE fleet-relevant but missing from FleetProfileApplier's knownKeys, list them by name with a one-line rationale for why each should be addable.
- Note any settings where adding them to FleetProfileApplier would need extra care (e.g. side effects, requiring a specific permission, or needing the app to restart) vs. ones that are a trivial addition.

This is a genuinely small, real research validation task for stayturgid's device-fleet tooling (Shizuku is the Android permission broker stayturgid depends on) -- not busywork, the findings are meant to inform whether/how to extend FleetProfileApplier next.
close_reason: Posted research recommendation: recommend not expanding FleetProfileApplier's knownKeys — existing 8 keys already cover the fleet-relevant surface; remaining settings are cosmetic, dead code, or security-sensitive and shouldn't be added

comments.author: Daniel JB Clark
comments.text:
# Research: which Shizuku settings does FleetProfileApplier miss?

## Method

Full preference surface enumerated from three places (all writing/reading the single
`SharedPreferences` store `ShizukuSettings.NAME = "settings"` — confirmed via grep, no
other `getSharedPreferences` call exists in `manager/`):

- `ShizukuSettings.java` — `Keys` class + a few raw string keys used directly (`mode`,
  `auth_token`, `lastPromptedVersion`)
- `manager/src/main/res/xml/settings.xml` — the actual Settings UI screen
- `SettingsFragment.kt` — wiring/side-effects for each preference

## Full settings/preference surface

| Key | Type | Currently in `knownKeys`? | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | int | yes | last launch method (unknown/root/adb) |
| `start_on_boot` | bool | yes | re-launch on boot |
| `watchdog` | bool | yes | watchdog service enabled |
| `tcp_mode` | bool | yes | ADB-over-TCP enabled |
| `tcp_port` | string(int) | yes | ADB-over-TCP port |
| `auto_disable_usb_debugging` | bool | yes | auto-disable USB debugging after start |
| `legacy_pairing` | bool | yes | legacy pairing dialog flow |
| `update_mode` | int | yes | off/stable/beta update channel |
| `language` | string (locale tag) | **no** | in-app UI locale override |
| `night_mode` | int | **no** | dark/light/follow-system |
| `black_night_theme` | bool | **no** | true-black dark theme variant |
| `use_system_color` | bool | **no** | Material You dynamic color (Android 12+) |
| `light_theme` | string | **no** | declared in `Keys`, read by `ThemeHelper.getTheme()`, **but has no writer anywhere** — dead/vestigial, no UI control sets it |
| `auth_token` | string | **no** | auth secret for authenticated start/stop intents |
| `lastPromptedVersion` | string | **no** | bookkeeping for the in-app "update available" nag dialog |
| `translation`, `translation_contributors`, `help`, `report_bug`, `category_advanced` | n/a | n/a | not stored values at all — these are `Preference` UI nodes that open a URL/dialog on click. Nothing to push. |

## Recommendation: do not expand `knownKeys`

The 8 keys `FleetProfileApplier` already knows about are, in practice, the complete
fleet-relevant surface. None of the other declared/stored keys belong in a pushed
profile:

- **`language`, `night_mode`, `black_night_theme`, `use_system_color`** — purely
  cosmetic UI state. Per `HANDOFF.md`, these fleet devices (Samsung S24, Pixel 7a, Fire
  HD8) run Shizuku headlessly under stayturgid's native agent; nobody looks at the
  Shizuku UI except during rare manual triage (e.g. the documented "Samsung process
  freezer" workaround, which requires opening the app once). There's no operator
  workflow where pushing a locale or theme across a fleet has value, and getting it
  wrong (see caveats below) has essentially no upside to offset the added surface area.
  Marginal exception: `language` could matter if triage screenshots need a consistent
  locale, but that's a "nice to have," not worth adding until someone actually asks for
  it.
- **`light_theme`** — don't add: it's currently unreachable dead code (no UI writer
  exists), likely a vestige from upstream Shizuku. This is a code-cleanup candidate,
  not a fleet-profile gap.
- **`auth_token`** — must NOT be added. It's a credential, not a config knob. It
  already has a dedicated, narrower provisioning path
  (`ProvisionAuthReceiver` / `PROVISION_AUTH` broadcast) that requires the caller to
  already possess the token. Folding it into `FleetProfileApplier`'s generic
  JSON-from-a-file/URI ingestion would mean any profile file dropped on
  `/sdcard/Download/` could silently overwrite the device's auth secret — a real
  security regression for no operational benefit.
- **`lastPromptedVersion`** — don't add: purely in-app bookkeeping for a UI dialog,
  meaningless to set from outside, and could actively misbehave the update-nag logic
  if force-set to a bogus value.
- **`translation`, `translation_contributors`, `help`, `report_bug`,
  `category_advanced`** — not settings at all (click-to-open-URL / click-to-open-dialog
  UI nodes), nothing to apply.

This is consistent with `HANDOFF.md`'s existing framing: "Shizuku's own fleet profile
remains for initial provisioning only, not ongoing operations" — the 8 known keys are
exactly the provisioning-relevant ones (launch mode, boot/watchdog behavior, ADB
transport, USB-debugging auto-disable, pairing mode, update channel). There isn't a
gap here worth closing.

## Caveat found along the way (existing known keys, not a missing-key issue)

Not something to fix as part of this research task, but worth flagging for whoever
picks up `FleetProfileApplier` next: `tcp_mode` and `tcp_port` are in `knownKeys` but
fall through to the generic `putValue()` branch (plain `SharedPreferences` write) —
unlike the Settings UI path (`SettingsFragment.kt`), which wraps changes to these two
in `maybePromptRestart` / `promptStopTcp` to reconcile the *running* ADB-over-TCP
listener (via `AdbStarter.stopTcp` / `ShizukuReceiverStarter.start`) with the new
preference value. Applying a profile that flips `tcp_mode` or changes `tcp_port` while
Shizuku is already running will update the stored preference but **not** the live
listener — they'll stay out of sync until the next manual/automated restart. If
`FleetProfileApplier` is extended further, this reconciliation gap (not scope of this
task, but same code path) is worth fixing at the same time. `start_on_boot` and
`watchdog` don't have this problem — `FleetProfileApplier` already calls through
`ShizukuSettings.setStartOnBoot()` / `setWatchdog()`, which carry the real side effects
(component-enabled-state change, `WatchdogService.start/stop()`).

## Answers to the specific questions

- **Full surface:** enumerated above — 8 known + 4 real-but-cosmetic + 1 dead + 2
  device-local bookkeeping/secret + 5 non-data UI nodes.
- **Fleet-relevant vs not:** only the existing 8 are fleet-relevant for this fleet's
  actual use case (headless provisioning). The 4 cosmetic ones are technically settable
  but have no operator use case today.
- **Missing-but-fleet-relevant list to add:** none recommended. If forced to pick one
  low-priority optional addition, it'd be `language` — but only if/when an operator
  actually asks for it.
- **Extra care needed if added anyway:**
  - `night_mode`, `black_night_theme`, `use_system_color`, `language` — trivial
    `SharedPreferences` writes technically, but the UI-driven paths also call
    `activity?.recreate()` / `AppCompatDelegate.setDefaultNightMode()` /
    `LocaleDelegate.defaultLocale = ...` to apply immediately; applied headlessly via
    `FleetProfileApplier` they'd only take effect the next time the UI is opened (low
    risk, just note the lag).
  - `auth_token` — security-sensitive, use the existing `PROVISION_AUTH` mechanism
    instead, never add to `FleetProfileApplier`.
  - `light_theme`, `lastPromptedVersion` — no legitimate reason to set externally.

title: Research: which process regenerates memory/codex/{memory_summary,raw_memories}.md?
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/djbclark/site-private/issues/4

SCOPE — RESEARCH/RECOMMENDATION ONLY, NOT A CODE-CHANGE TASK. Do not edit home-agents.md, memory/codex/memory_summary.md, memory/codex/raw_memories.md, or any other file in the repo. Do not run any Codex CLI commands that could mutate memory state (read-only inspection of Codex config/docs/scripts is fine and expected). Deliverable is a recommendation posted as a GitHub issue comment. Do not close the issue.

Context: site-private/memory/ is the one exception to the worktrees-only rule (agents commit memory directly to master in place, one-fact-per-file so concurrent writers don't collide). memory/codex/memory_summary.md and memory/codex/raw_memories.md are rewritten whole-file and caused the only merge conflict in the 2026-07-26 site-private PR #3 merge. home-agents.md currently labels them 'owned/regenerated artifacts' but nobody has confirmed which process actually regenerates them.

Questions to investigate and answer with a clear recommendation (not just present tradeoffs):
- Which Codex process/command/script (re)generates memory_summary.md and raw_memories.md? Manual consolidation step, scheduled job, or a side effect of a specific Codex memory command? Look at ~/.codex/config.toml (site-private/codex/config.toml is the live source per repo convention), any Codex memory-related scripts/hooks in this repo, and Codex's own docs/CLI help if accessible.
- Are these files meant to be hand-edited at all, or always regenerated from the per-fact files/raw_memories?
- What's the intended concurrency story if multiple agents touch Codex memory concurrently — single owner regenerates, or last-writer-wins?

Post findings as a comment on https://github.com/djbclark/site-private/issues/4. If you can confirm the answer, say so plainly; if you can't fully confirm it from what's inspectable in this repo, say what you found and what remains unknown rather than guessing.
close_reason: Posted findings as GitHub issue comment: memories are a native Codex CLI feature (features.memories/generate_memories, stable, no manual subcommand), files are Codex-owned regenerated exports (not hand-edited), and concurrency is last-writer-wins per machine/session — see issue #4 comment

title: Research: dispositions for stayturgid issue #151's untracked Termux-family apps
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/djbclark/stayturgid/issues/151

SCOPE — RESEARCH/RECOMMENDATION ONLY, NOT A CODE-CHANGE TASK. Do not modify ansible_collections/stayturgid/android_common/roles/bootstrap_apks/ or any other config. Do not run any commands against actual fleet devices (adb/ssh/etc) — desk research and reasoning about existing issue content only, unless read-only device inspection is unambiguously safe and non-disruptive. Deliverable is a recommendation posted as a GitHub issue comment. Do not close the issue.

Context: PR #194 already landed com.termux.x11 pinning (the actively-used one). This issue's remaining, still-open scope is the other 7 untracked Termux-family/third-party packages found on fleet devices via live pm list packages (p7a, 2026-07-30):
- com.termux.tasker (0.9.0), com.termux.styling (0.32.1), com.termux.window (0.17.0), com.termux.widget (0.15.0) — official Termux-family, no version pin/checksum/update coverage currently.
- io.github.swiftstagrime.termuxrunner (1.7.2), com.gardockt.termuxterminalwidget (1.3), com.maazm7d.termuxhub (3.2.4) — third-party, unclear provenance (installer=null on all of them, likely Obtainium leftover).

Open questions to research and answer with a recommendation (not just present tradeoffs):
- For each of the 3 third-party apps: what does the app actually do, is it still useful/needed, any red flags (abandoned, security concerns, better alternatives)? Recommend keep-and-lock vs remove for each.
- Is com.termux.window distinct from com.termux.x11 in a way that matters, or does one supersede the other? (Both were found installed simultaneously.)
- For whichever apps are recommended to keep: sketch what a bootstrap_apks lock entry would need (gh_repo/gh_tag/gh_pattern/checksum, resign:true if unsigned) — don't write the actual ansible changes, just specify what's needed so a follow-up implementation task can act on it directly.
- The issue also asks that whatever solution is chosen make it easy to add future Termux companion apps, not just backfill the current gap — note any structural suggestion for that, but don't implement it.

Post findings as a comment on https://github.com/djbclark/stayturgid/issues/151.
close_reason: Posted research/recommendation comment on stayturgid#151: recommend keep-and-lock com.termux.window (found load-bearing in tests/device_tier.py and termux_userland role), remove all 3 third-party apps (no codebase references, headless-fleet context), and structural fix for GitHub-only lock/update-check tooling

title: Research: should AI-context-pack generation (Repomix or alternative) be wired into the ops release mechanism?
description:
GitHub issue: https://github.com/djbclark/site-djbclark/issues/35

Summary: git ls-files+tiktoken / repomix token counts gathered across all 3 repos (stayturgid ~1.05-1.16M, site-djbclark ~0.2M, site-private ~0.07-0.08M tokens). Proposal: wire an AI-context-pack generator (Repomix or alternative) into just ops-release-check/ops-release-deploy so each tagged ops-vX.Y.Z release ships a versioned context snapshot as a release asset.

Open questions to resolve (this is a RESEARCH task — produce a recommendation, not a release-mechanism code change, unless the recommendation is to implement and that's confirmed separately):
- Release-time trigger vs CI-on-merge-to-master vs on-demand only?
- One pack per repo or one combined pack for the 3-repo suite?
- Plain vs --compress (or both)?
- Artifact location: GitHub Release asset vs committed to repo vs generate-on-demand only?
- Should pack-generation failure block a release, or just log/warn?
- Also evaluate alternatives to Repomix: gitingest, code2prompt, yek, Aider's repo-map, MCP-based context servers (LLM Context, Repo Prompt) — issue notes we're mostly targeting Claude Code sessions which already have on-demand file-reading/search tools, so worth questioning whether a static full-repo pack is even the right primitive.
- Flag risk of staleness, secret/vault-file leakage, and release-artifact storage bloat.

The issue includes a ready-to-paste second-opinion prompt for a fresh/differently-sourced AI session — see the GitHub issue body for the exact text if useful.

Deliverable: post findings/recommendation back as a comment on https://github.com/djbclark/site-djbclark/issues/35 (do not close the issue without explicit confirmation).
close_reason: Posted research findings/recommendation as comment on issue #35: recommend against wiring context-pack generation into the release mechanism (decoupled, on-demand instead); evaluated Repomix/gitingest/code2prompt/yek/Aider repo-map/MCP context servers; flagged staleness/secret/storage risks

description:

SCOPE — TRACKED ONLY, DO NOT ACT: this is a tracking-only issue. Do not modify, commit, discard, delete branches on, or otherwise touch ~/src/Shizuku. Do not run destructive git operations there. If asked to work this task, the correct action is to report current status (re-check branch/commit-count/diff) as a comment here, nothing else.
